glossary.definition: An unaged tequila class. In other spirits the same words can mean different classes or nothing legal at all; class terms are spirit-specific.
Mezcal's unaged class; joven can also be used informally elsewhere (this app marks non-legal uses as editorial labels).
Wood-rested classes with spirit-specific minimums; tequila rules do not transfer to mezcal or raicilla.
A mezcal made with fruit and/or a raw chicken or turkey breast suspended during a (usually third) distillation — a specific production tradition, not a spirit category of its own.

A batch made from multiple agave species, typically harvested and fermented together. An ensamble needs composition evidence; it is not simply a post-distillation blend, and it is not a separate spirit family.
An aged spirit filtered (often through charcoal) to remove color while keeping some wood character. It is a finishing choice, not a legal class in most categories.
The Norma Oficial Mexicana number on the label identifying the certified producer. NOMs identify the maker; absence of a NOM (as with uncertified tuxca) means uncertified, not lower quality.
Regional words for a small distillery: vinata in Sonora, taberna in Jalisco raicilla country, palenque in Oaxaca. Same function, different tradition.
Small producers label batches; batch details (agave mix, ABV, maker) can differ materially between bottles of the same brand. Batch-specific facts must not silently become brand-wide facts.

A composition claim about fermentables. It is distinct from quality and from eligibility for this app: agave-based traditions with disclosed non-agave fermentables (some comiteco) are included honestly.
